title: Grade 7 Science — Wed, Jun 11
description: Fibre to Fabric — Day 3 of 5: Silk — sericulture and production
subject: science

questions.question: The rearing of silkworms to produce silk is called:
questions.explanation: Sericulture is the practice of raising silkworms (Bombyx mori) and harvesting their silk cocoons.

questions.question: Silk fibre is made from the cocoon of the:
questions.explanation: The silkworm spins a cocoon around itself using a single continuous silk thread. The cocoon is harvested for silk.

questions.question: The silkworm feeds on:
questions.explanation: The Bombyx mori silkworm feeds only on mulberry leaves. Mulberry trees are specially grown for sericulture.

questions.question: The process of extracting silk thread from the cocoon is called:
questions.explanation: Reeling is the process of unwinding the long silk thread from the boiled cocoon onto a reel.

questions.question: Why are cocoons boiled in hot water before reeling?
options: To kill the silkworm inside and soften the gum holding the thread
To add colour to the silk
questions.explanation: Boiling softens the sericin gum binding the silk thread and kills the pupa inside, allowing the thread to be unwound.

questions.question: The stages of the silk moth's life cycle in correct order are:
questions.explanation: The life cycle is: Egg → Larva (silkworm feeds and grows) → Pupa (spins cocoon) → Adult silk moth.

questions.question: One silk cocoon can yield a thread of silk that is approximately:
questions.explanation: A single silk cocoon contains a continuous filament of 300–900 metres of silk thread!

questions.question: Mulberry silk is the most common type of silk. Which silkworm produces it?
questions.explanation: Bombyx mori feeds on mulberry leaves and produces the finest, most common type of silk — mulberry silk.

questions.question: Tasar silk is produced by silkworms that feed on:
questions.explanation: Tasar silkworms (Antheraea mylitta) feed on oak, arjun, and other forest trees. Tasar silk is used for upholstery.

questions.question: Muga silk is mainly produced in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Muga silk is the golden-coloured silk unique to Assam. It has a natural golden shine and is extremely durable.

questions.question: Silk has a natural sheen because:
options: It is dyed with gold paint
The triangular prism-like structure of silk fibre refracts light
questions.explanation: Silk fibres have a triangular cross-section that acts like a prism, bending light and giving silk its characteristic lustre.

questions.question: Which Indian city is most famous for producing fine silk sarees?
questions.explanation: Kanchipuram in Tamil Nadu is famous for its high-quality silk sarees. Varanasi (Banaras silk) is also renowned.

questions.question: The gum-like substance that binds silk fibres together in the cocoon is called:
questions.explanation: Sericin is the natural gum protein that holds the silk filament together in the cocoon. It is removed during processing.

questions.question: Silk is a protein fibre. The main protein in silk is called:
questions.explanation: Fibroin is the structural protein of silk. It makes up the strong, fine filament of the silk thread.

questions.question: Eri silk is unique because:
options: It comes from an insect that eats mulberry only
The silkworm is not killed — the moth emerges first (open-ended cocoon)
It is produced only in Karnataka
questions.explanation: Eri silkworms spin open-ended cocoons, allowing the moth to emerge. This 'ahimsa silk' does not require killing the silkworm.
